# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🖐 👈 👉 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

## Thinking

What I see on the bomb: display 0, red light, embossed sign "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", three wires (1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue). Nobody can act on this but Blind, and nobody can look it up but Mute.

Tracing the channels: I can't hear, so Mute's only route to me is gestures — that's exactly what arrived: three signed messages from Mute and one wave from Blind. Crucially, Mute can *hear* me even though Mute can't talk, and Blind can hear me too. So speech is my high-bandwidth channel to both at once; gestures to me are Mute's only channel back, and I am the relay for anything that must go Mute → Blind, since Mute can't speak and Blind can't see signs.

Guessing at Mute's signs: [👋 ✍] looks like "hello, the manual/writing"; [☝ ✌ 🤟] reads as 1-2-3, quite possibly asking or confirming the three wires; [🫵 🖐 👈 👉 🙏] is probably "you, describe it, please" — left to right. My speech answers all three at once, so I won't over-trust those readings.

Plan: dump a complete verbal inventory of the bomb to both (words carry colour names fine — Blind just can't *see* colour, and Blind can read the embossed sign by touch). Propose a small gesture vocabulary to Mute in words while making the gestures in the same breath, so each sign is paired with its meaning. Then answer Mute the simple way: thumbs-up for "received", and 1-2-3 for "yes, three wires". And freeze Blind: nobody cuts until Mute has the manual entries.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am Deaf. I can see the bomb and I can speak, and you can hear me; I can never hear you, so from now on answer me only in gestures. Everything on the bomb, top to bottom: a display reading 0. A light, red. An embossed sign reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires in a row: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, numbered left to right, 1 at the left end. Look up all four things: the display, the red light, the embossed sign, and the three wires. Until you say otherwise nobody touches anything. Let us fix a sign code now, each sign shown as I say it: thumbs up 👍 means yes, thumbs down 👎 means no, pointing finger ☝ means wire 1, victory ✌ means wire 2, love-you hand 🤟 means wire 3, pinching hand 🤏 means cut, writing hand ✍ means the manual, waving 👋 means hello. So cut wire two would be ✌ then 🤏. Confirm or amend by gesture. I am gesturing to you right now: thumbs up, then one-two-three — meaning yes, I received your signs, and there are three wires.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I am Deaf. I see the bomb and I am speaking, so you hear me directly; I cannot hear you, but Mute can hear you. Do not cut or press anything yet. The bomb, as I see it: a display showing the numeral zero. A light that is red. An embossed sign reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, which you can read under your own fingers. Three wires side by side: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, numbered from one end to the other. Feel whether the wires carry numbers and find which end is 1, then tell Mute out loud, since Mute hears you and holds the manual. Mute cannot speak; Mute will answer me by gesture and I will relay any instruction to you by voice. Your wave reached me; I can see your hands, so gesture to me any time, but keep anything important in words for Mute. Nobody acts until Mute has found these modules in the manual.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ☝ 🤏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## Thinking

Arrivals this turn: Mute sent [👍], then [👎 ✍], then [✍ ☝ 🤏]; Blind sent [👍]. Blind's thumbs-up is almost certainly acknowledgement of my spoken briefing — Blind hears me directly, so that channel works. Mute's chain, in my proposed code, reads roughly: "yes — no, [regarding] the writing — the manual: wire 1, cut." Two candidate readings: (a) the manual says cut wire 1 (green) and the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign is a decoy, or (b) something subtler about the sign having no manual entry. These readings do not diverge trivially — one of them ends with scissors on a green wire — and my gestures are the *only* path that instruction can take to Blind, with no second attempt if I relay it wrong.

So: no cutting this turn, whatever the true answer is — nothing on the board suggests time pressure (display has sat at 0 for two rounds), and a wrong cut kills all three. Instead I run a yes/no confirmation protocol with Mute, who hears my speech and answers in signs, one answer per question in fixed order: is it exactly one wire; is it wire 1 green; is the embossed sign a decoy; what about the display-0 and the red light. I echo Mute's own sign string back as the first question, add 👌 as a question marker, and ✋ as "hold." Blind gets the cautious relay: probable meaning stated as uncertain, explicit instruction not to act, and a request to describe everything tactile aloud to Mute — especially the printed wire numbers and which end numbering starts from — since Blind's findings can only reach me laundered through Mute's gestures.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I read your signs as: the embossed sign is no good, and the manual says cut wire 1, the green one. Cutting is fatal if I have misread you, so confirm before anyone acts. Answer in exactly this order, one sign per question, thumbs up for yes and thumbs down for no. One: does the manual say to cut exactly one wire? Two: does it name that wire as wire 1, green? Three: does the manual say the embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE is a decoy or should be ignored? Four: does the manual cover the display showing zero? Five: does it cover the red light? Then, if the true instruction really is cut wire 1, end with the pinch sign followed by the one finger. If it is something else, end with the raised open hand, then the correct instruction in our code. Blind will not touch anything until I relay a confirmed order, so take your time and be precise.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf again. Mute's signs suggest the manual says to cut wire 1, the green one, and that the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE warning may be a decoy. That is my reading of hand signs, and it is not confirmed. Do not cut anything yet; I will relay the order only after Mute confirms it through a yes-and-no exchange. Meanwhile, speak aloud for Mute everything your hands find: the display, the light, whether each wire carries a printed number, which end the numbering starts from, and the exact wording of the embossed sign. Mute hears you, holds the manual, and will answer me by sign. Also mention any button, switch, panel or moving part you can feel that I have not listed from my side.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✍", "☝", "🤏"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## Thinking

Mute answered my five questions in exact order — yes, yes, yes, no, yes — and closed with the terminal code we agreed: pinch, then finger-one. Decoded: exactly one wire to cut, it is wire 1 (green), the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign is a decoy per the manual, the display entry doesn't exist, the red light does have an entry. The instruction is internally consistent three ways over (Q1, Q2, and the closing code all agree), so I'm treating "cut wire 1" as confirmed.

The one remaining fatal risk is local, and it's mine to fix: Blind must map "wire 1" onto a physical wire without eyes, and my earlier phrasing "1 at the left end" was from *my* side of the bomb — mirrored for Blind. Facing the upright sign, Blind's right is my left, so wire 1 is the **right-hand** wire from Blind's perspective. Better anchors: if the numerals are tangible, cut the one that feels like a 1; otherwise, the end of the bomb where the embossed sentence *ends* (the WIRE end) — the sentence's start fixes orientation without any appeal to left/right.

So I relay the confirmed order now with that airtight identification, freeze everything else afterward, and queue up the loose ends with Mute: what the red-light entry actually demands, whether anything must follow the cut, and whether display 0 is benign. Mute gets a sign echo that the order was received and relayed. Blind gets no gestures — they'd land as blanks anyway; my voice is Blind's only line to me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. The order is confirmed by Mute through our coded exchange: cut exactly one wire, wire 1, the one that is green on my side. Here is how you find it without eyes. First choice: if the wires carry printed numerals you can feel under your fingers, cut the one numbered 1. Second choice, if the numbers cannot be felt: the embossed sign is printed to read as a normal sentence; find the end of the bomb where that sentence finishes, the end with the word WIRE. Wire 1 is the outermost wire at that end. Put plainly: from your side, facing the sign, the sentence starts on your right and wire 1 is the wire nearest where it ends. Cut only that one wire, as close to its base as your tools allow, and touch nothing else. Before you cut, say aloud for Mute which wire you have chosen and how you identified it. After the cut, take your hands off the bomb completely and wait: the red light and the display showing zero are still unresolved, and I will relay any further step. Mute is listening to everything you say and will answer me by sign.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I received all five answers and the closing code. Understood as: exactly one wire, wire 1 green, the embossed sign is a decoy, no manual entry for the display, and the red light does have an entry. The cut order for wire 1 is relayed to Blind with instructions to identify it by tactile numeral or by the end where the embossed sentence finishes, and to announce the choice aloud to you before cutting. Three questions for next round, answer thumbs up or thumbs down in this order. One: does the manual entry for the red light require any action from us? Two: after wire 1 is cut, does the manual require any further step? Three: is a display showing zero a normal or harmless state? If anything urgent comes up outside those questions, wave and then sign it in our code. Thank you — your discipline with the protocol is what made this safe to relay.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤏", "☝"])
```
